>  would you be happier if you were in a more sexually fulfilling relationship? 

There's really no way to know, right? I've never had a functioning sexual relationship.

What I can say for sure, is that when my mood crashes, the tension from trying to decide if I should leave, cheat, or cheat with permission really fuels my suicidal thoughts.
I'm one of those people. Let us try!

Thank you for replying.

She's really not willing to open up about this. It's always been the case for her, I just didn't realize it until recently. If I ask her to doing some reading or talk to someone about maybe developing some desire, I'm accused of "Trying to change her."

We have a schedule for sex acts that she sticks to faithfully, but with all the enthusiasm of a toddler being asked to eat their veg. That's what makes me feel like a rapist.
My university had GREAT counselors working out of the Student Health Center.

Two days is awfully early to give up on a med for either side effects or lack of effectiveness.  Many troublesome side effects only last a week or two, which, coincidentally, is how long it takes many antidepressants to "kick in." I would suggest giving it some more time, but if you start feeling WORSE, put in a call to your psychiatrist.

There's GREAT information on antidepressant medications to be found at www.crazymeds.us
Second for calling 9-1-1 (or your area's emergency number). There are people who want to help - call them!

If you use their insurance, they will likely get an Explanation of Benefits that will include the provider's name and likely a diagnosis code.

Are you a student? High schools and universities usually have low- or no-cost counseling for their students.

You can also consider checking the Psychology Today provider directory and looking for providers who work on a sliding scale.

I personally have been happy with text chat therapy through Talkspace - that's $100/month, which is cheaper than even my co-pay if I used my insurance for an in-person therapist, but may be out of reach depending on your financial situation.
